museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales
title: Art Gallery of New South Wales: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works move between open country, city streets and the people given a place within them.
introduction:
A broad landscape can make its people seem incidental. A railway station can scatter them across wet ground, while a ceremonial picture may organise every body into a rank. This selection invites attention to those choices of scale and placement, from Streeton's river valley to a small family under towering ferns.

The views are made, not simply found. Colour can bring a coast into order, a reflected tree can close a billabong, and columns can organise an imagined ancient court. Portraits offer a counterweight: a face and a few held gestures can claim the space that landscape elsewhere gives to hills or sky. The guide traces those changes without treating the selection as a complete account of the collection.
visitNote: Check the gallery's collection pages and current displays for individual locations. This selection includes paintings and works on paper, whose display schedules may differ.

books.title: The Elements of Drawing
books.author: John Ruskin
books.note: John Ruskin's Elements of Drawing offers exercises in looking at trees, water, light and distance. Read it beside the landscapes here as a historical drawing manual, not as a guide to Australian history.

works.title: Still Glides the Stream, and Shall for Ever Glide
works.catalogueTitle: Still glides the stream, and shall for ever glide
works.medium: Oil on canvas, later mounted on hardboard
works.credit: Arthur Streeton. Still glides the stream, and shall for ever glide. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Full source frame, proportional resize and JPEG compression. https://www.wikiart.org/en/arthur-streeton/still-glides-the-stream-and-shall-for-ever-glide-1890
works.description: The winding river prevents the valley from settling into stacked horizontal strips. Its changing width establishes depth while nearer trees interrupt, but do not close, the prospect. Streeton makes an expansive view readable through one continuous route. The picture's space depends on this constructed relation between an obstructed foreground and an open distance, rather than on openness alone.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: The Railway Station, Redfern
works.credit: Arthur Streeton. The railway station, Redfern. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Full source frame, proportional resize and JPEG compression. https://www.wikiart.org/en/arthur-streeton/the-railway-station-redfern-1893
works.description: Wet ground connects people who remain separate in the street. Their dark bodies repeat below as reflections, spreading movement across the grey foreground. Smoke and damp air soften the railway buildings, so solid architecture does not dominate the scene entirely. Weather changes the city's visual structure, making transient surfaces as important as the station's permanent forms.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: From My Camp (Sirius Cove)
works.credit: Arthur Streeton. From my camp (Sirius Cove). WikiArt source label: Public domain. Full source frame, proportional resize and JPEG compression. https://www.wikiart.org/en/arthur-streeton/from-my-camp-sirius-cove-1896
works.description: The cove begins with individual rocks close at hand, then opens toward small boats on blue water. A steep wooded bank limits the view, concentrating attention at the meeting of shade and sunlight. Streeton gives this harbour scene a more bodily scale than the broad river prospect. Distance remains present, but it must be approached through a specific piece of shore.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Antibes
works.credit: John Russell. Antibes. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Yellow cliffs, pink buildings and green sea establish the coast before any small detail becomes necessary. Russell lets broad colour areas distinguish foreground, settlement and water. Their contacts do much of the work an outline might otherwise perform. The place stays recognisable while the surface remains an arrangement of emphatically separate painted passages.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Rough Sea, Morestil
works.credit: John Russell. Rough sea, Morestil. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The strokes turn around coastal rocks with the moving water. Their changes of direction keep the blue-green surface unsettled even where a complete wave cannot be isolated. Russell distributes motion through the paint rather than concentrating it in one spectacular crest. Dark rock provides the resistance against which that mobile surface can be understood.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Mon Ami 'Polite
works.credit: John Russell. Mon ami 'Polite. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Blue passes through beard and clothes into the sea behind, giving portrait and coast a shared handling. The long tool and the man's firm grip nevertheless keep his body distinct within that texture. Russell connects a person to a place without dissolving either into the other. A practical object provides the pose with its clearest direction.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: The Parish Hall
works.credit: Dorrit Black. The Parish Hall. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Pointed roofs and straight walls meet a curved path and clipped green garden forms. Dorrit Black simplifies the view by preserving those differences rather than by giving every surface equal detail. Windows repeat the architecture's angular rhythm. The building retains its character because a few chosen relations between garden and structure remain specific.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Elizabeth Street, Sydney
works.credit: Dorrit Black. Elizabeth Street, Sydney. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The tracks supply a curve through compressed blocks of red, cream and green. Tilted buildings and trees make the street's movement a property of the whole arrangement, not merely of vehicles or pedestrians. Black removes much incidental description while retaining the forces that direct a city view: routes, repeated angles and the interruption of one mass by another.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Naval Funeral
works.credit: Dorrit Black. Naval Funeral. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Dark hats and white crosses repeat across a red field, turning bodies into the ordered units of a collective ceremony. Individual figures remain visible, but rank determines their relation to one another. The picture's regularity belongs to its subject. A funeral's shared public form is made legible through the suppression of freely chosen positions and movements.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: David's First Victory
works.credit: William Strutt. David's first victory. Image credit: William Strutt (1825 - 1915) – creator Born in Teignmouth, Devonshire, England. Died in Wadhurst, East Sussex, England. Details on Google Art Project; Source credit: rAHycKA0dYmQBg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: David's bare legs stand above the mass of the fallen lion, whose mane occupies the near ground. The unequal scale gives the feat its immediate terms: a smaller body has overcome a larger one. The raised hand completes the staged account of victory. Strutt makes the biblical episode comprehensible through proportion before detailed narrative explanation is supplied.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Fern Gully with Aboriginal Family
works.credit: Thomas Clark. Fern gully with Aboriginal family. Image credit: Thomas Clark (circa 1814 - 1883) – creator Born in London, England. Died in South Yarra, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Details on Google Art Project; Source credit: OQESJm1KWLE8pw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The Aboriginal family occupies a small part of a gully dominated by arching ferns. That reduced scale directs attention toward vegetation, but it does not make the land uninhabited. Reading a colonial landscape requires holding those two facts together. The painter's distribution of space is a choice about visibility, not a neutral measure of whose presence matters.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: A Billabong of the Goulburn, Victoria
works.catalogueTitle: A billabong of the Goulburn, Victoria
works.credit: 1835-1907, Henry James Johnstone. A billabong of the Goulburn, Victoria. Image credit: H.J. Johnstone (1835 - 1907) – creator Born in Birmingham, Warwickshire, England. Died in London, England. Details on Google Art Project; Source credit: pgHo2TGml7JaNw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Reflected trees extend the dark bank downward, deepening the enclosure around still water. A pale opening beyond becomes unusually important because so much of the view closes around it. Johnstone uses reflection to construct space rather than simply repeat objects. The picture's principal route into distance remains narrow, held between the framing trees and their doubles.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Stalagmites, Burragalong Cavern
works.credit: Conrad Martens. Stalagmites, Burragalong Cavern. Image credit: Conrad Martens (1801 - 1878) – creator Born in London, England. Died in North Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. Details on Google Art Project; Source credit: WQHbDtXpn1ifAQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Light catches irregular stone edges, allowing formations to emerge separately from the cavern's darkness. A small figure supplies a measure that the underground view would otherwise lack. Martens gives enclosed space the recession of a landscape. What can be seen depends on a few illuminated boundaries rather than on the broad light of an open sky.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Self-Portrait
works.credit: Nicholas Chevalier. Self portrait. Image credit: Nicholas Chevalier; Source credit: https://www.artgallery.nsw.gov.au/collection/works/945/. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Chevalier's wide hat enlarges the silhouette while much of his face remains in shadow. Eyes, cheek and beard receive enough light to establish a likeness without equal clarity everywhere. The dark mass surrounding those features sends attention back toward them. The self-portrait demonstrates how selective illumination can concentrate presence rather than simply withhold information.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Portrait of Inez Bensusan
works.credit: Cecil William Rea. Portrait of Inez Bensusan. Image credit: Cecil William Rea died 1935; Source credit: https://www.artgallery.nsw.gov.au/collection/works/OB1.1968/. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The gathered hands anchor the lower part of the green-clad figure, while Bensusan's head turns away from the body's direction. That small difference keeps the pose from becoming fixed in a single line. Rea gives the lit face room to act independently of the settled posture. The portrait's activity lies in this modest adjustment rather than in overt gesture.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Waiting
works.credit: Gordon Coutts. Waiting. Image credit: Gordon Coutts; Source credit: 6wGRrRzA1P4jEA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The title identifies an interval, but gives no certain account of what will end it. Hands rest on the chair while the pale dress catches window light. The landscape continues beyond the room, offering a direction the seated figure does not follow. Coutts sustains the pause through the relation between an available view and a body remaining still.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: The Visit of the Queen of Sheba to King Solomon
works.catalogueTitle: The visit of the Queen of Sheba to King Solomon
works.credit: Sir Edward John Poynter. The visit of the Queen of Sheba to King Solomon. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/edward-poynter/the-visit-of-the-queen-of-sheba-to-king-solomon-1890
works.description: Repeated columns provide a framework for an abundance of steps, costumes and assembled figures. Poynter's imagined ancient court needs that order to make the royal meeting locatable within the spectacle. Architecture is an active narrative device here. It distributes attention and establishes rank, rather than merely supplying an elaborate background behind the principal actors.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Snowdrop and the Seven Little Men
works.catalogueTitle: Snowdrop and the seven little men
works.credit: John D. Batten. Snowdrop and the seven little men. Image credit: Own work sailko. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The heroine's long sleeping body lies across the foreground, slowing the arrangement of smaller figures behind. Warm reds and golds connect them to a decorated interior. Batten gives the fairy tale a held moment instead of continuous action. The contrast between the horizontal sleeper and the gathered observers allows stillness itself to organise the scene.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: Mucius Scaevola
works.credit: Matthias Stom. Mucius Scaevola. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/matthias-stom/mucius-scaevola
works.description: The hand held over the flames is both the action and the source of the scene's illumination. Light spreads from that test of endurance across faces and clothing before reaching darkness. Stom concentrates the Roman story's moral claim into a small, exposed part of the body. The surrounding gathering witnesses an act whose physical cost remains central.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

works.title: At Lilydale
works.credit: Louis Buvelot. At Lilydale. Image credit: Louis Buvelot (1814 - 1888) – creator Born in Morges, Switzerland. Died in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Details on Google Art Project; Source credit: swHxc1c_UePU6w at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Cut branches and uneven ground complicate the foreground before the track opens toward fields and hills. Buvelot gives the settled prospect a worked surface close at hand. The landscape is therefore more than a smooth view into distance. Its near edge retains traces of material alteration, making the route outward begin among things that have been handled or cut.
works.museum: Art Gallery of New South Wales

closingSections.title: Notice what the scale leaves small
paragraphs: Return to a landscape and locate its people, routes or signs of work before following the distant view. The image may give them less space than their importance warrants. This selection is not a guide to current gallery rooms; confirm the display of individual works with the museum before making a visit plan.
